questions.question_text:
One of the angles in an isosceles triangle is $154^{\circ}$.
What are the sizes of the other two angles?

options.why: Subtracted $154^{\circ}$ from $180^{\circ}$ but gave the entire remainder to each equal angle instead of dividing it by two.
Divided the given $154^{\circ}$ angle by two instead of dividing the remaining $26^{\circ}$ by two.
Used $360^{\circ}$ instead of $180^{\circ}$, then divided $360^{\circ}-154^{\circ}$ by two.

questions.solution_text:
$2x+154=180$
$2x=26$
$x=13^{\circ}$, so the other two angles are $13^{\circ}$ and $13^{\circ}$.
$154^{\circ}$ cannot be one of the equal angles, because $154+154>180$.

questions.solution_text:
$BC$ is a transversal cutting the parallel lines $DBE$ and $AC$.
$z$ and $\angle BCA$ lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of $BC$, so they are alternate angles and therefore equal.

questions.question_text:
One of the angles in an isosceles triangle is $87^{\circ}$.
Which option gives both possible pairs of other angles?

options.why: Considered only the case where $87^{\circ}$ is the angle between the equal sides, overlooking the case where it is an equal base angle.
Considered only the case where $87^{\circ}$ is an equal base angle, overlooking the case where it is the angle between the equal sides.
In the first case, gave each equal angle the whole remainder $180^{\circ}-87^{\circ}=93^{\circ}$ instead of dividing it by two.

questions.solution_text:
If $87^{\circ}$ is the angle between the two equal sides:
$2x+87=180$
$2x=93$
$x=46.5^{\circ}$.
If $87^{\circ}$ is one of the two equal angles:
$x+87+87=180$
$x=6^{\circ}$.
The other angles are $46.5^{\circ}$ and $46.5^{\circ}$, or $87^{\circ}$ and $6^{\circ}$. Both cases are possible because all angles are positive and each set totals $180^{\circ}$.
